verses.text: That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes, that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life
(and the life was revealed, and we have seen, and testify, and declare to you the life, the eternal life, which was with the Father, and was revealed to us);
that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son, Jesus Christ.
And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled.
This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie, and don’t tell the truth.
But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

footnotes.content: John wants us to know: he was *there*. Not a distant theory, but something his hands touched, his ears heard. When someone old tells you they have met the risen Lord, listen to their presence, not their perfection. That steady witness carries weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The life that comes from the very heart of God took on flesh and walked among us. John calls us to see what he saw—that eternal life was not far off in heaven, but was here, tangible, with the Father and revealed to us. The mystery is that simple and that close.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fellowship—real friendship with God and with each other—that is the point of all the announcing. Jesus did not come just to be remembered. He came so we could be *together*, in the same room, so to speak, with the Father and with one another. That is the offer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: John writes so that our joy will overflow. Not a grim duty, then, but a full cup running over. When someone reminds you of the truth about Jesus and you feel your heart lift, that is the Spirit's work—the filling that makes writing about faith worth the trouble.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: *God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.* That one sentence—the core message—means no shadow in His heart, no hidden ill will, no corner where He plots against you. When you are afraid that God is secretly angry, remember: light all the way through. This is the message the whole letter hangs on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A hard word: claiming fellowship with God while living in the dark is a lie. Not a flaw or a weakness—a lie. John does not soften it. But notice he is not accusing *us*—he is warning us, which means there is time to turn, to step into the light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Walking in the light is not perfection; it is honesty. And as we do—as we tell the truth about ourselves and stay close to Jesus—His blood cleanses us. The remedy is already flowing. We do not have to get clean first; we get clean *by* staying in His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If we claim we have no sin, we are only fooling ourselves. Age teaches you this: the longer you live, the more you see your own smallness. Pride in our own goodness is the last self-deception to go, and it keeps the truth out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Confession—simply naming what is true—opens the door. God is faithful: He will not pretend the sin was not sin. But He is also righteous, which means He *can* forgive without winking at wrong. The blood of Jesus stands between us and judgment. Tell Him the truth, and watch Him keep His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this: we live in a time when many voices say 'no absolutes,' 'trust your own truth.' But if we say we have never sinned, we make God a liar. He is more honest than our age allows. His word—the call to repentance and grace—is still in us only when we let it be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
